title: Justice Department Files to Intervene and Dismiss Lawsuit that Would Hamper America’s AI Innovation and Security

reading.body:
The summary attached to this incident is not a summary of the incident. It is a message from a document processing step saying it could not read a supplied PDF, that the file appeared corrupted or improperly encoded, and asking for the text in another form. The failure sits in the ingestion step, before any summarization of the reporting, and it takes the shape of a model asserting a property of the source document as fact on the strength of its own failed extraction.

That text was written into the incident record and published without a human check, so a reader is told the document is unreadable rather than that the tool could not read it. Catching it would have taken a check that separates a broken source from a broken parser, and a review step before generated text is stored as the description of a record.

The five reports listed concern a gas turbine power plant serving a data center, a notice of intent to sue under the Clean Air Act, a complaint filed by the NAACP and others, and a Justice Department filing to intervene and dismiss. None of that is established by this record, because the record's own summary failed to extract it, and a notice of intent to sue is not a finding of violation, a complaint is not a verdict, and a motion to dismiss is not a ruling.
